title: [CQ-F04] Durable revision authorization
description:
Objective: Stamp daemon-owned approvedPlanRevision atomically in human approval paths and invalidate stale associations without deleting history.

Deliverable: Durable revision authorization. This is task F04 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): F03.
definitionOfDone: A delayed approval cannot authorize a newer contract.
Strict callers cannot omit approval revision; malformed tokens never become legacy omission.
Existing legacy approvals remain explicitly legacy, not inferred strict approvals.
Fresh verification `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the durable daemon-owned slot at the existing write boundary. Add `approvedPlanRevision?: number | null` beside Task.planRevision: a safe-integer number identifies a revision-checked approval, null marks an explicitly unchecked legacy approval, absence is historical/unknown legacy provenance. Neither null nor absence authorizes strict execution; status or planApprovedAt never backfills the slot. Strip it from every ordinary updateTask patch; createTask's explicit construction must continue to ignore supplied values. Extend ONLY taskStore.updateTask's existing private daemonOwned parameter with approvedPlanRevision (do not expose it on StateManager's public update signature). For PLAN_APPROVED, derive the canonical planRevision first, then choose the trusted internal value or null, validate a numeric value using the existing revision decoder and require equality to that derived revision before writing. Suggested core: `const approved = daemonOwned?.approvedPlanRevision ?? null; ... updated.approvedPlanRevision = approved;` Ordinary caller updates, even with a PLAN_APPROVED event, must never mint a number. For that approval event, after the existing readiness check, require a numeric token when resolveTaskExecutionProfile(settings, task.executionPolicySnapshot) is verified-local; omission is INVALID_INPUT on expectedPlanRevision. Reuse the existing profile resolver, never deliveryPolicy or a new strictness flag. Do not change assertExecutionProfileReady or its current EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY error precedence. Material plan/DoD/contract changes advance only planRevision and KEEP the old approvedPlanRevision, timestamps, amendment history and other evidence: inequality invalidates the association without erasing history; progress/equal-contract/metadata writes keep both revisions. Test all three material surfaces, a no-op/progress control, same-write combined edits, reload, and attempted forge/null/erase through ordinary store updates. An injected first task writeEntity failure must leave disk/map/events/activity unchanged. No schema migration or second revision counter.

Wire the two human paths to the trusted store argument, not a public patch. In taskStore.approveTask keep status validation and the supplied-token safe-integer/CAS checks under the caller-held state mutex; retain the decoded reviewed revision and pass it (or null for a permitted legacy omission) to the local updateTask function with PLAN_APPROVED and the internal daemonOwned argument. Compare BEFORE any mutation; never substitute a newly fetched revision for a stale supplied token. The single persisted image contains status, planApprovedAt and approvedPlanRevision. Move cancelSpeedModeTimeout after the successful update so an injected primary task-write failure also retains the pending timer; queued timer callbacks remain serialized by the existing mutex. Do not promise cross-entity rollback if a later worker write fails. Add approvedPlanRevision to the WS UPDATE_TASK denylist; APPROVE_TASK and board-drag delegation continue to share approveTask and top-level expectedPlanRevision, ignoring other drag updates. Add real-wire forge/erase/create cases, primary-write failure with no published approval, duplicate/concurrent approvals (one success only), and timer-preservation controls. Strict-omission regression: in narrowly scoped tests only, spy on assertExecutionProfileReady to make it a no-op, then prove live verified-local and stored verified-local floor still refuse missing tokens with INVALID_INPUT and zero writes; restore spies in cleanup. Real unmocked strict requests must still return EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY (existing executionPolicySnapshot.test.ts unchanged). This tests the future authorization guard without enabling or certifying strict execution. Error handling: keep current malformed-token and mismatch codes and WS context allowlist; no new approval MCP tool. Automatic SPEED/TURBO stamping/rearming remains F05; relaxed set_task_status PLAN_APPROVED without the internal revision remains explicitly legacy/null.

Update only the Plan approval compare-and-swap section for F04's downstream contract: numeric/null/absent provenance, exact rendered token, atomic persisted authorization, stale-number retention and safe-integer-plus-equality validity, daemon-owned denial of forged updates, and the effective-profile strict omission rule behind the still-closed readiness gate. Explicitly distinguish both human WS paths from token-free relaxed set_task_status and the not-yet-fenced SPEED/TURBO paths owned by F05. Do not claim all approval paths are fenced, nor execution/claim/completion enforcement (F06-F08). Document no backfill from planApprovedAt/status and no change to legacy/observe delivery policy. The broader SCHEMA/PLAN_APPROVAL_FRESHNESS sweep belongs to F12; record these precise hand-forward items in the completion handoff rather than editing contested unrelated docs.

Single verification gate: from the repository root run exactly `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` fresh after the final implementation, require exitCode 0, and retain command/outputTail for complete_task. This full daemon gate is mandatory because the Task shape and approval protocol are shared surfaces; existing held-out assertions must pass unchanged and the F05 timer test stays skipped until F05. Use native dependencies matching the lockfile: on WSL/Linux a source-identical temporary snapshot with Linux-only PATH and MOE_* removed avoids inherited Windows executables; never install over shared Windows node_modules. Record snapshot source identity and any owned-file overlays so QA can reproduce it; preserve existing CRLF/LF and peer dirty bytes on Windows/macOS/Linux. No generated/dist changes, no manual .moe edits, and no agent Git-write commands; wrappers alone land.

Final, single adversarial-self-review of the F04 diff. Try stale/future/zero/null/omitted/non-finite tokens, caller-forged or erased approval stamps, a contract edit queued ahead of approval, two competing approval messages, a primary task-write failure with an armed timer, and a project rollback beneath a stored strict snapshot. Check no path infers numeric approval from status/time/event name, no material edit relabels the old number as current or deletes history, and progress stays non-material. Mutation-check the task's focused assertions in a disposable source copy by dropping the durable stamp, accepting a stale token, allowing forged updates, and dropping the strict omission guard; each must fail its corresponding test (the guard case uses only the scoped readiness stub).
